content.en: Saheli was set up six years ago in 1981, by a small group of women. Our experiences with anti-dowry campaigns and issues related to rape, women's health and legal rights, through the seventies, made us aware of the urgent need to provide space and opportunity to individual women to rebuild their lives. The brutality and violence against women prevalent in our society, deprive women of the right to live with dignity and self-respect. Changing patterns of family, clash of values, compounded by economic pressures have made women victims of growing mental and physical torture.

Saheli Women's Resource Centre is a place women come to, to find the means to live a dignified life. Over 500 women have come to us in the last six years, seeking help. Our attempt is to share our experiences, and collectively seek solutions to our problems. A woman's desire to confront her situation and assert herself, is half the battle. We give courage to every woman struggling to emerge from the crisis in her life, to stand on her own, in the knowledge that she is not alone.
Providing support to individual women takes up a substantial portion of our time. In addition, in the coming year we intend to do the following:

en.text: ★ Hold discussions, talks and seminars on women’s right and status.
★ Research into the working conditions of women employed in the informal sector.
★ Campaign around issues of health, emphasizing a woman’s right to make conscious choices.
★ Find out attitudes towards domestic violence, so as to create awareness on this issue.
★ Involve ourselves in civil rights issues.

content.en: With these activities we hope to reach out to women in the neighbouring slums, to university students, working women and housewives, and hope to raise their awareness.

When we started, we had no money. With donations of Rs. 80/- and contributions from friends, and volunteers giving their time, we struggled to keep Saheli open six days a week. We functioned from a garage donated by a volunteer.
Since then we have grown, and so have our needs for funds. While a number of us are contributing our time and money for Saheli work, we still need money for our office and five full time workers.

Since the beginning, we have relied on individual support rather than institutional, foreign and governmental funds for carrying out our activities. This we feel helps us remain responsible to all who contribute their resources. It also helps us to remain independent of various pressures on our values which are invariably exerted by institutional donors, including that of making us complacent.

For the coming year, we need Rs. 10,000/- a month to pay office rent, support five full time workers and to meet administrative and other expenses. We need your financial support for this cause. We value every rupee you give with sympathy and concern.
Contributions to Saheli are eligible for exemption u/s 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
